title: Cut value of the encoded graph
statement: Let $E$ be any finite list of ordered pairs of natural numbers, let $F$ label the vertices indexed below the variable bound of $E$ by Boolean values, and let $f:\mathbb N\to\{0,1\}$. Suppose $F(v)=f(v)$ at every such vertex. In the weighted directed graph formed from $E$, the cut value of $F$ equals the number of entries $(u,v)$ of $E$ with $f(u)\ne f(v)$, divided by the length of $E$; repeated entries are counted with multiplicity, and when $E$ is empty both sides are interpreted by the displayed real quotient.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ is an arbitrary finite list of pairs of natural numbers, possibly empty and with repetitions.
$F$ is a Boolean labeling of the graph's bounded vertex set.
$f$ is a Boolean-valued function on the natural numbers.
